manifest.name: dsh-task-dispatcher
manifest.description: Task dispatcher for DeepSeek Harness: use TickTick (滴答清单) as the daily task dispatcher — a cordis timer pulls today's due tasks, writes them to the workspace task file, and notifies (WeChat via ClawBot / flomo / macOS) so the agent works through them and writes results back to TickTick

scripts.test: node tests/smoke.mjs && node tests/deferred.mjs && node tests/cheap.mjs

bundle.text:
# dsh-task-dispatcher bundle patch: inserts the plugin row into the profile roster.
# Applied as a profile bundle layer (declared by the `dsh.bundle.patch`
# manifest field in package.json). Activate with:
#
#   # local development (link)
#   dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-task-dispatcher
- insert:
    - id: task-dispatcher
      name: dsh-task-dispatcher
      config:
        announceToAgent: true   # 在系统提示中公告插件（能力 + 今日任务文件路径）
        enabled: true           # 插件总开关
        dispatchIntervalMinutes: 30   # 每隔多少分钟自动从滴答清单拉取一次（0 = 关闭定时）
        autoExecute: false      # 是否自动执行：为每个拉到的新任务单独开一个 DSH 会话去执行（串行）
        retryCooldownMinutes: 60 # 失败任务重试冷却分钟
        projectName: "5️⃣AI"      # 任务来源清单（按名称解析）
        dueMode: "today"         # today = 今天到期/逾期；all = 全部未完成
        includeUndated: true     # 是否包含无截止日期任务
        notifyFlomo: true        # 有任务变化时推送 flomo
        flomoTag: "AI/DSH/派发"   # flomo 标签
        notifyMac: true          # 有任务变化时 macOS 通知
        cheapMode: false         # 省钱模式：勾选后自动执行只在 DeepSeek 空闲/优惠时段开跑
        cheapPreset: "official-2026" # 时段口径：official-2026（官方现行）/ legacy-utc / custom
        cheapStrategy: "wait"    # 高峰期策略：wait = 排队等到下个空闲开始；skip = 本轮跳过
        cheapMarginMinutes: 0    # 尾部余量分钟（0 = 关闭尾部保护；建议 15 或 workerTimeoutMinutes）
        cheapTimezone: "Asia/Shanghai" # 解释高峰时段的 IANA 时区

readme.text: Use TickTick (滴答清单) as DSH's daily task dispatcher: a cordis timer pulls today's due tasks from the configured source list (default `5️⃣AI`; point it at `In progress` to dispatch from the "doing" list), writes them to today's task file, and notifies via **WeChat (ClawBot)**, flomo, or macOS (configurable). The agent reads the file, works through the items, and writes results back to TickTick with `ticktick_complete`.
> Reuses the already-installed `dsh-ticktick` plugin (its data layer + OAuth credentials in `~/.dsh/dsh-ticktick.json`) — no duplicate configuration.

- **Interval dispatch**: cordis `ctx.interval` polls every minute and dispatches when the configured interval (minutes) has elapsed; 0 disables the timer; `dispatcher_run` dispatches manually anytime.
- **Task source**: default the `5️⃣AI` list (set it to `In progress` to dispatch from the "doing" list; `projectName` / `projectId` configurable); `dueMode=today` pulls due-today/overdue + undated, `dueMode=all` pulls all incomplete.
- **Today task file**: writes a Markdown checklist (default `~/.dsh/dsh-task-dispatcher/today-tasks.md`).
- **Execution-result receipts (`notifyResult`, on by default)**: every auto-executed task pushes a SHORT outcome message (`OK`/`FAIL` + title + a one-line result, or the failure reason such as a worker timeout) as soon as its worker settles, plus a compact batch tally when a pass runs more than one task - a run reports back by itself instead of relying on the worker calling `dispatcher_report`. The summary is the worker's **stdout final answer** (progress/reasoning go to stderr), stripped of ANSI and the `DONE` marker and capped at 220 characters.
- **Notify on change only**: `notifyWechat` (WeChat, relayed through the local [DSH-WeChatClawBot](https:

Requires **DeepSeek Harness ≥ 0.1.5-rc.1** (declared as `dsh.engines.dsh` in the package manifest, so the DSH plugin marketplace can report it) and is verified against **0.1.5-rc.1**. This build carries the DSH 0.1.5 adaptations: the strict tool-result contract (lossless-JSON snapshot, `additionalProperties: false` schema validation, and `output.render` returning `ContentBlock[]`) plus executable resolution that survives a launchd-started host whose `PATH` is only `/usr/bin:/bin`. **Since this version** the `peerDependencies` range explicitly declares compatibility with **DSH 0.2.0-rc.2** (`^0.2.0-rc.2` is now included), so no compatibility warning appears on 0.2.0-rc.2. No functional change.
> The shape is **install → restart → confirm it loaded**. Every step states the expected result, so you can tell success from failure.

1. **Install the plugin**: run `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-task-dispatcher` in a terminal.
   Expected: the command exits cleanly and `dsh-task-dispatcher` shows up in the dependencies of `~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json`.
2. **Restart DSH**: restart `dsh web` (sidebar “restart”, or re-run the same start command).
   Expected: the GUI comes back with no plugin-loading errors in the startup output.

> 📷 **【Screenshot slot 2】proves the plugin actually installed**
> How to capture: in the terminal, stop right after step 1's command finishes (or on the DSH startup lines after the restart); crop: the terminal window
> Redact: **local absolute paths, your username, any token**
> To fill in: save the shot to `docs/images/dsh-task-dispatcher-01-installed.png`, then replace this whole block with
> ``

3. **Confirm it loaded**: ask the agent to run `dispatcher_status` (or check that “Task dispatcher” appears on the settings page).
   Expected: output starts with `插件状态：已启用` / status “enabled” and lists the source list, pull interval and notification channels.

4. **Open the settings page**: DSH Web → **Settings** → expand the **“Task dispatcher”** card.
   Expected: you see the master switch, pull interval, task source, notification channels and auto-execute blocks.

> 📷 **【Screenshot slot 4】proves where the settings live (the step people get stuck on)**
> How to capture: Settings → stop on the top half of the expanded “Task dispatcher” card (master switch + pull interval + source list)
> Redact: workspace paths / list names if they carry personal information
> To fill in: save the shot to `docs/images/dsh-task-dispatcher-02-settings.png`, then replace this whole block with
> ``

5. **Adjust what you need**: set the **task source** (default `5️⃣AI`; use `In progress` to dispatch from the “doing” list), the **pull interval** (0 disables the timer), the **notification channels** (WeChat ClawBot / flomo / macOS; WeChat is off unless you switch it on) and **auto-execute** (each task then runs in its own headless session).
   Expected: the status line refreshes after saving and `dispatcher_status` reports the same values.
6. **Turn on cheap mode** (optional; the headline of this release): in the same card, tick **“省钱模式（自动执行只在 DeepSeek 空闲时段开跑）”** (off by default), then pick the **preset** (default “official, Mon–Fri 09–12 / 14–18 peak”), the **strategy** (default “wait for off-peak”, or skip) and the **tail margin** (set it to your worker timeout, e.g. `15` / `30`).
   Expected: a **peak-window editor** appears, and the status line shows “current window / next run / queued tasks”.

> 📷 **【Screenshot slot 6】proves cheap mode is configured correctly**
> How to capture: Settings → “Task dispatcher” → stop on the fully expanded cheap-mode area (toggle + preset + strategy + tail margin + window table)
> Redact: none (just keep the workspace path at the top out of frame)
> To fill in: save the shot to `docs/images/dsh-task-dispatcher-03-cheap-mode.png`, then replace this whole block with
> ``

7. **Trigger one dispatch**: ask the agent to run `dispatcher_run`, or press **pull now** in the panel; to “run once right now even in peak”, press **“省钱模式（高峰也马上执行，仅本次）”**.
   Expected: today's task file `~/.dsh/dsh-task-dispatcher/today-tasks.md` gains items (the agent reads it and works through them), and you get one notification when the task set changed.
8. **Look at the result**: run `dispatcher_status`, or read the status line in the panel.
   Expected: “last pull: <time> · <N> items”; with cheap mode on during peak you also see “queued: N” and “next run: <time>” — **tasks held back for the next off-peak window is exactly what cheap mode looks like**.

> 📷 **【Screenshot slot 8】proves it is actually in use (the most important one)**
> How to capture: after one dispatch, stop on the panel status line, or on the “last pull / queued / next run” lines of `dispatcher_status`; crop: just that card or that terminal output
> Redact: **real task titles, local paths, WeChat display name** — use a throwaway test task
> To fill in: save the shot to `docs/images/dsh-task-dispatcher-04-in-use.png`, then replace this whole block with
